text:
When Vancouver's coverage needs something good to say about the losing, it tends to land on Liam Ohgren. CBS Sports wrote "Game taking step forward" in early November, and Vancouver Hockey Daily had him shining "in another Canucks loss" after he scored in Winnipeg on Nov 5. The 22-year-old Swede, a 2022 first-round pick of Minnesota, has 6 goals in 20 games.

Our numbers say enjoy the goals, but don't build on them yet. He has scored 6 times on 3.15 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 21% after 9% last season, and over his last ten games his chances have been normal for him while his ice time fell 2:18 a night. The harder problem is five on five, where Vancouver has had only 37.6% of the expected goals with him on the ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 53% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so he needs the puck moving the other way. Our range has him finishing somewhere between 12 and 21 goals.
headline: Ohgren's goals are real, his chances are ordinary
